categories.main_business_segments: Expedia Group operates through three main segments: B2C, B2B, and trivago. The B2C segment includes consumer-facing travel brands such as Expedia.com, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, and others, offering a wide range of travel and advertising services. The B2B segment provides travel technology and supply solutions to partners like airlines, travel agents, online retailers, and financial institutions. The trivago segment operates a hotel metasearch platform generating advertising revenue by referring users to travel service providers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Expedia leverages a unified technology platform that supports its brands and partners, utilizing proprietary software, APIs (such as Rapid), and cloud infrastructure. The company has migrated its core B2C brands onto a single front-end stack to enable faster product innovation, scalability, and efficiency. Machine learning and artificial intelligence are increasingly integrated into product development, customer service, and marketing optimization. The company also provides direct connect technology for suppliers and maintains both legacy data centers and cloud-based systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Expedia serves a broad range of customers including individual leisure travelers, families, and small groups through its B2C brands, as well as business partners such as airlines, travel agents, online retailers, and financial institutions via its B2B segment. Major end markets include lodging (hotels and alternative accommodations), air travel, car rentals, cruises, activities, and travel insurance. The company also targets advertisers seeking access to travel audiences through its media and metasearch platforms.
categories.geographic_coverage: Expedia operates globally, with a strong presence in the United States and significant operations in Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and other international markets. The company’s brands and services are available in nearly 50 countries, with localized offerings and websites. The U.S. remains the largest revenue contributor, but international markets are a key focus for expansion and growth.
categories.supply_chain_position: Expedia primarily operates as an intermediary in the travel supply chain, connecting travelers with suppliers such as hotels, property owners, airlines, car rental companies, and cruise lines. It aggregates and distributes travel inventory from suppliers to end customers and business partners, functioning downstream as a distributor and marketplace rather than as a direct provider of travel services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Expedia’s strategic priorities include leveraging its unified technology platform for faster innovation, expanding its global supply and brand presence, and deepening direct customer relationships. Key R&D initiatives focus on AI and machine learning, enhancing the customer experience, and developing configurable, scalable technical capabilities. The company is also investing in loyalty (One Key program), global market expansion, and B2B technology solutions.
categories.revenue_model: Expedia generates revenue through three primary models: the merchant model (facilitating bookings and acting as the merchant of record, primarily for lodging), the agency model (acting as an agent and earning commissions or fees, mainly for air and some hotel bookings), and the advertising model (earning fees from advertisers and metasearch referrals). In 2024, merchant, agency, and advertising/media/other accounted for 69%, 23%, and 8% of total revenue, respectively.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Expedia faces intense competition from global online travel agencies (OTAs) such as Booking Holdings (Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda), Airbnb, and Trip.com, as well as from travel suppliers’ direct channels, metasearch engines (e.g., Google, Kayak, TripAdvisor), and traditional travel agencies. Expedia is positioned as one of the world’s largest OTAs with a broad portfolio of brands and a leading B2B travel technology platform, but faces ongoing pressure from supplier-direct channels and new entrants leveraging AI and alternative business models.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Expedia reported $13.7 billion in revenue, a 7% increase from 2023, with gross bookings of $110.9 billion (up 7%). The company’s B2B segment is experiencing the fastest growth (21% revenue growth in 2024), while B2C remains the largest segment by revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 billion, and net income attributable to Expedia Group was $1.2 billion. The company has a large global scale, with a healthy but normalized post-pandemic growth trajectory and ongoing investments in technology and market expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Expedia emphasizes its broad and deep travel supply, global brand portfolio, and unified technology platform as key differentiators. The company offers customers a wide selection of travel products, competitive pricing, and a unified loyalty program (One Key) that spans multiple brands and product types. For suppliers and partners, Expedia provides access to a large global audience, advanced technology solutions, and data-driven merchandising tools. Its ability to combine multiple travel components and offer cross-brand rewards enhances customer retention and engagement.
